adequacy_evidence.quote: Scientific adequacy is **supported**. The report's conclusion is appropriately bounded to the supplied participant-level cope maps and the fixed upstream model. Its one-sided one-sample sign-flip max-t test controls familywise error over the 90%-support whole-brain mask; it also checks the all-participant intersection, uses the vmPFC box only for localization, and explains the standardized gain modulator and absent participant variance maps. The methods and caveats support the reported absence of whole-brain-corrected positive vmPFC evidence (canonical content/workspace/analysis.py, SHA-256 eafd08b16a91aa973d2c952f2e4b86739fae814d4374d2fad64af167434851d8; content/workspace/results/summary.json, SHA-256 2a688886cf26a86397175b17663647cb2c26c77ad43e5ce779fbb0bc6c190f8e; content/workspace/results/group_p_fwe.nii.gz, SHA-256 f7c4e55c60d25683db8f2190438e005ad5dadb82473038cf3292a1e938d36461).

hypothesis_conclusion.quote: The supplied gain-effect estimates did **not** support a positive vmPFC response to increasing potential gain.
